children: Tunisia and the African Development Bank (AfDB) have signed two financing agreements totalling about $240 million to modernise drinking-water infrastructure in Greater Tunis and rehabilitate ageing production facilities operated by state-owned Tunisian Chemical Group (GCT).
The agreements were signed in Tunis on 22 September 2026, AfDB said in a press statement.

The first comprises a €111.5 million loan, backed by a state guarantee, to national water utility Société Nationale d’Exploitation et de Distribution des Eaux (SONEDE) for the Greater Tunis Drinking Water Network Technical and Energy Performance Improvement Project (PAP-GT).
The project aims to improve the reliability and efficiency of potable water supply for nearly 2.9 million people in Greater Tunis.

Works include the rehabilitation of 25 kilometres (km) of transmission pipelines and 113km of distribution networks, modernisation of three water distribution facilities and deployment of leak-detection equipment.
The project also includes 17 megawatts (MW) of solar power capacity, energy-recovery turbines at pressure-breaking facilities and upgrades to electromechanical equipment.
A digitalisation component will involve the installation of 120,000 smart meters, serving around 500,000 people, as well as remote metering and management systems.

The second agreement provides a $110 million loan, also backed by a sovereign guarantee, to GCT for the Environmental Upgrading and Rehabilitation Support Project for the Tunisian Chemical Group's Production Units (PAER-GCT).
The financing will support GCT's broader investment programme to restore production capacity, modernise management systems and improve the environmental and energy performance of its facilities.
Investments will cover GCT sites in Gabès, Skhira and M’Dhilla, including treatment of atmospheric emissions, modernisation of critical installations and energy-efficiency improvements.
At the Gabès site, the recovery of available steam is expected to provide 23MW of self-generation capacity.
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)
